result:
Now I have the full picture. Here's what happens when an org owner downgrades a workspace plan.

## Who may do it

The mutation is `changePlanAction` in `src/actions/billing/change-plan.ts`, which wraps a handler with `withAction(changePlanSchema, ...)` (`src/actions/_lib/with-action.ts`). `withAction` first resolves the `Actor` (`getActor`/`requireActorFor`, `src/lib/actor.ts`) from the session and the `orgId`/`orgSlug` in the input, then hands control to the handler, which immediately calls `can(actor, "org:manage_billing", { kind: "billing", orgId })` (`src/lib/permissions.ts`). `ROLE_MATRIX["org:manage_billing"]` requires role `"owner"`, so `explain()` only returns `granted_by_role` for an owner (or a platform-staff bypass). If the check fails, `changePlanAction` throws `ForbiddenActionError` before anything else runs. The service layer (`changePlan` in `src/server/services/billing-service.ts`) re-asserts the same rule with `assertCan`, so the owner-only gate is enforced twice — once in the action, once in the service — independent of which caller invokes it.

## What is compared before the downgrade is accepted

Inside `changePlanAction`, after the permission check, `assertPlanFitsCurrentUsage(actor, input)` runs: it calls `getUsage(actor, orgId)` (`src/server/services/usage-service.ts`, backed by `usageRepo.getUsage`) to get today's `seatsUsed`/`projectsUsed`/`storageMbUsed`, and `getPlanLimits(input.plan)` (`src/config/plan-limits.ts`) for the **target** (smaller) plan's ceilings. For each resource it calls `wouldExceedLimit(input.plan, resource, used, 0)` — a zero-delta check, i.e. "does what's already in use still fit the new plan?" If any resource would overflow, it throws `PlanLimitError` and the action stops before touching the database. The service function `changePlan` in `billing-service.ts` repeats the same loop over `SUMMARY_RESOURCES` (`seats`, `projects`, `storageMb`, `webhooks`) as a second, defensive gate.

## Where the plan is recorded, and which value is authoritative

Only after both checks pass does `changePlan` call `subscriptionRepo.updateSubscriptionPlan(orgId, plan, interval)` (`src/server/repositories/subscription-repository.ts`), which updates the `subscriptions` row (`src/server/db/schema/billing.ts`) — setting `plan`, `interval`, and forcing `status` back to `"active"` (a plan change also ends any trial).

There is a second, separate `plan` column on the `organizations` table (`src/server/db/schema/organizations.ts`), set once at creation in `organization-repository.ts`. The comment in `billing-service.ts` (`planFor()`) asserts that the `subscriptions` row is "the authority" and `organizations.plan` is "only a display convenience." That's true for the handful of call sites that go through `billing-service.ts`'s `planFor()`/`checkLimit()` (the billing summary page, `assertWithinLimit`). **It is not true for the rest of the app.** I checked every other consumer of a plan value, and they all read `org.plan` straight off `orgRepo.findOrgById()` — the `organizations` table column — never the subscription: `project-service.createProject`, `issue-service` (issues-per-project quota), `webhook-service` (both the `webhooks` quota and the `isEnabled("webhooks", …)` flag gate), `attachment-service` (storage quota), `invitation-service` and the `invite-member`/`accept-invitation`/`create-project`/`create-issue`/`create-webhook`/`update-seats` actions, `feature-flag-service.buildFlagContext` (feeds `plan: org?.plan`), `usage-service.recomputeUsage`, and the `cleanup-archived-job`/`webhook-delivery-job` retention/webhook jobs.

Crucially, **`changePlan()` never writes to `organizations.plan`** — no code path does; I grepped every `orgRepo.updateOrg` call site and none of them touch `plan`. So a downgrade updates the authoritative-sounding `subscriptions` row but leaves the denormalized `organizations.plan` column exactly as it was.

## What happens afterward

`changePlan` emits `billing.plan_changed` via the event bus (`src/lib/event-bus.ts`). Two subscribers react: `activity-service.ts` records an activity-log entry ("Plan X → Y"), and `webhook-service.ts` enqueues an outbound webhook delivery for the org's endpoints. Back in the action, `revalidateTagged([orgTag(orgId)], CACHE_PROFILES.hours)` invalidates cached data tagged for that org so `getBillingSummary` (which does read the subscription correctly) shows the new plan and usage meters immediately.

## What behaves differently away from the billing pages — and what doesn't

Because of the split above, the billing page itself is correct (it reads `subscriptions` via `planFor`), but everything that reads `organizations.plan` keeps enforcing the **old, bigger** plan's limits and feature set after a downgrade: project/issue/seat/storage quotas in `project-service.ts`, `issue-service.ts`, `invitation-service.ts`, `attachment-service.ts` still allow the old ceilings; `webhook-service.ts` still treats webhooks as enabled/at the old quota; and `feature-flag-service.buildFlagContext` still evaluates plan-gated flags (`isEnabled` with a `"plan"` strategy, via `planAtLeast` in `plan-limits.ts`) against the pre-downgrade plan, so features like `activity_feed`/`digest_email`/`webhooks`/`issue_templates` (growth-and-up) or `advanced_search`/`ai_issue_summary` (enterprise-only) stay lit up for a downgraded org everywhere except the billing screen. Separately, the plan-aware rate limiter (`src/lib/rate-limit.ts`) is unaffected either way in practice, since its `setOrgPlan()` setter is never called anywhere in the codebase, so it always falls back to the `"free"` bucket size regardless of plan.
